fixes.explanation: Not quite, baker. Nobody in this scene is waiting on a calendar. The LORD says, "I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me. If not, I will find out." (Genesis 18:21). He's going to look for Himself. I've seen people put off a dentist visit for a whole year, but that's not what's happening here.

That's a real title, friend, but Abraham doesn't use it here. "The Shepherd of Israel" shows up in Psalm 80:1. Abraham says, "Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?" (Genesis 18:25). His question is about judging, so the title he speaks is Judge.

Other way around, friend. Abraham asks about the fifty lacking five, and the LORD replies, "If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it." (Genesis 18:28). So with forty-five, the city is not destroyed. The statement is true.

Fifteen is a good guess, baker, but Abraham isn't that low yet. After thirty, he says, "…suppose twenty are found there?" (Genesis 18:31). He's still bargaining, and he's not done. And the LORD answers, "On account of the twenty, I will not destroy it." Fifteen has to wait its turn, and it never gets one.
